concepts.def: Shaping tempo, dynamics, articulation and phrasing to communicate the character and style of a piece rather than merely reproducing its notes.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit A2 1: Performing — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit A2 1: Performing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit A2 1: Performing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the most effective way to fix a fast passage that keeps going wrong?
options: Play it repeatedly at full speed
Practise it slowly and increase the tempo gradually
Leave it out and hope for the best
Only ever play complete run-throughs
The loudness of your playing
The accuracy of tuning of the pitches you produce
The speed of the piece
The order of the programme

mcqs.q: Stylistic awareness in a performance means what?
options: Playing every piece in the same way
Applying the conventions of the piece's period and genre
Always adding vibrato
Choosing the hardest piece available

mcqs.q: If you make a small slip during a performance, the best response is to do what?
options: Stop and restart the piece
Keep going and maintain the pulse
Apologise to the audience
Slow down for the rest of the piece

mcqs.q: Is a top-mark performance simply one with no wrong notes?
options: Marks are awarded mainly for how difficult the outfit and stage presentation are.
A perfect performance just means playing all the right notes in the right order.
No - accuracy matters, but marks also reward interpretation, stylistic awareness, tone and communication with the listener.
Practising means listening to recordings instead of playing.

mcqs.q: What is the best general strategy for practising a piece?
options: Practising means playing the piece straight through from the beginning every time.
Work in a targeted way: isolate difficult sections, practise them slowly, then reassemble the piece.
Marks are awarded mainly for how difficult the outfit and stage presentation are.
Practising means listening to recordings instead of playing.

mcqs.q: Are 'intonation' and 'tone quality' the same thing?
options: Marks are awarded mainly for how difficult the outfit and stage presentation are.
No - intonation is the accuracy of tuning, while tone quality describes the timbre or sound colour you produce.
Intonation means the volume level of the performance.
Intonation just means having a nice sound.

free_texts.hint: Starts with the first subject in the tonic.

sequence.def: First match repertoire to your strengths and the time requirement
Isolate and slow down difficulties before running the piece
Add dynamics, articulation and phrasing once notes are fluent
Complete run-throughs with accompanist/backing before recording
Perform the programme in one sitting for assessment
Last: send recording and documentation to the exam board
